A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoViP work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning and personalization experiments, ablations, caption-quality evaluations and a human preference study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds multi-image benchmark evaluations, a distilled SFT comparison and qualitative visual-degradation examples.

M1.justification: The core rewards, GSPO optimization, degeneration filtering and CAG remain unchanged. Appendix G adds a distillation extension: RL-trained CoViP generates verified personalized captions used to train a Qwen3-VL-8B student through LoRA SFT.

E1.justification: v2 adds MM-NIAH, MMNeedle, MuirBench and MMIU, extending evaluation to general multimodal retrieval, needle localization and multi-image semantic, temporal and spatial understanding. Figure S.6 also introduces degraded-input examples. The earlier personalization datasets and diagnostic tasks remain.

E2.justification: Tables S.8 and S.9 add Qwen3-VL-8B trained by SFT on CoViP-generated captions as a comparator on the existing captioning and downstream tasks. The previous proprietary, zero-shot, RAP and RePIC comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Retained experiments keep their stated settings. Added evaluations specify approximately 2.8K MM-NIAH samples, a 1K MMNeedle subset with 4x4 grids, 1.3K answerable MuirBench questions and 11K MMIU questions. The new SFT control uses 3K teacher-generated captions.

E4.justification: v2 adds an RL-versus-distilled-SFT analysis, qualitative tests involving lighting, occlusion, resolution and clutter, and task-level analysis contrasting identity-retrieval gains with spatial-reasoning failures. These address substantive additional questions beyond the retained reward, optimizer, concept-count and prompt ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added results continue point-estimate reporting without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original numerical results are retained. New Table S.3 reports CoViP gains over Qwen3-VL-8B of 1.3, 4.0, 2.0 and 1.5 percentage points on MM-NIAH, MMNeedle, MuirBench and MMIU, respectively. New SFT results are mixed: SFT exceeds CoViP on four-concept captioning, 63.2 versus 59.7, and direct LAR, 40.0 versus 34.8, while trailing in the other reported settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, reward definitions, GSPO derivation, Algorithm 1 and supplementary equations are unchanged. The additions introduce empirical evidence and discussion rather than new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about contextualized visual personalization, captioning as a proxy task, RL post-training, CAG and downstream personalization gains.

C2.justification: New Appendix E substantially expands limitations concerning synthetic-to-real transfer, noisy or conflicting memories, annotation and privacy barriers, and visual robustness. Appendices F and G add interpretations about broader visual transfer and RL necessity, alongside an SFT-tuning caveat; Figure S.10 identifies weaknesses in 3D reasoning.

D1.justification: v2 documents the 3K-caption distillation dataset, teacher and student models, LoRA training and added benchmark sample/grid configurations. Existing implementation details and prompts remain. The abstract's Project Page link changes from a GitHub repository to a project website.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mei et al. (2026) to the personalization discussion and cites the four newly evaluated multi-image benchmarks. The existing comparison with prior personalization approaches and the principal novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 reorders the observations in Section 5.2, expands the LAR explanation and inserts a dedicated Further Limitations appendix, renumbering subsequent appendices. Most existing prose remains unchanged; the LAR rationale is partly duplicated.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with four new appendix tables and five figures covering data limitations, visual variations and failures, external benchmarks and SFT comparisons. Original displays are retained, with several relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The external benchmark comparisons and explicit applicability limits strengthen empirical support and transparency beyond v1's existing evidence. The SFT control is useful, but its acknowledged limited tuning and mixed outcomes do not establish the new claim that RL is essential for generalization, particularly when SFT wins on direct LAR. The additions therefore provide a limited net quality improvement.
